items.note: Aggregate placeholder for webbing, water, rations and small kit until M2.5 itemises it; rifle, magazines, helmet and vest are separate items.
Empty magazine mass published. See docs/research/ballistics.md (values from search extracts of the cited pages).

10-round magazine of the SVD (Wikipedia, search extract, medium). Empty mass about 0.21 kg is a game value (low). Holds the light-ball 7.62x54R the PKP fires (the 7N14 sniper round is not modelled: no difference in the game's ballistics).
Belt box of the AGS-30 (M7.6d): 29 rounds (Wikipedia; sources give 29 or 30, medium); about 14 kg loaded: the empty box and belt of about 4 kg is a game value (low).

AGS-30 30 mm automatic grenade launcher on its tripod (M7.6d): 16 kg unloaded, 17.5 kg with the sight (Wikipedia, GunRF, search extracts, medium), carried by the team's gunner. The crewServed block: set-up 40 s, packing 15 s, crew 2 (Army Recognition: gunner and ammunition carrier, medium), the fewest who can still fire 1, sight 0.7 m (the gunner sitting behind the low tripod), traverse +-30 deg before a 4 s re-lay, 2 s to lay, engages men on its own out to 1200 m (point targets about 800 m, sight range 1700 m: medium): game values otherwise (low). Direct fire only (high-angle fire deferred).
1.0-1.25 kg, pistol and fragment protection (game value: 2.5 mm steel equivalent). See docs/research/squads.md.
About 7.5-8 kg; plates rated against rifle rounds (class given as Br5/Br6 depending on source), soft armour around them. Plate coverage of the chest is a game value. See docs/research/squads.md.

Under-barrel 40 mm grenade launcher, about 1.5 kg. The search tool declined these look-ups in the research session; values are from general published references as remembered and must be verified against a public source. Game abstraction.
100-round belt in its box (published belt length); box mass and tracer mix are game values. Links counted in the empty mass.
RPG-7V2 launcher with sight, about 6.3 kg (from memory of published figures). Fires the PG-7VL (ammunition.json, M7.4a).

Two litres of water in canteens or a bladder (M11.6: a charged item, charge in ml; 2000 ml full). The 1.6 kg of the full item is kept: 0.8 g per ml folds the canteens into the water (water is 1 g/ml; empty canteens ~0.1-0.15 kg each, unsourced estimate): low, owner to review.
One day of rations. Mass is a typical value, not sourced; part of the itemised load that replaces the placeholder.

The pouch of the individual first-aid kit; its contents are counted items since M10.1 (a rubber tourniquet, two IPP-1 dressings, haemostatic powder, a pain-relief syringe tube: 0.6 kg with the pouch, the old placeholder mass). 2011-model Russian kit contents from nordsint.org and CNA 2024 (search extracts; quantities one each, low).
Load-carrying vest or belt kit, pouches, small pack, weather clothing, tools. Mass is a typical value, not sourced; part of the itemised load that replaces the placeholder.

Night-vision goggle; used by sensors in M9. Mass is a typical value, not sourced; part of the itemised load that replaces the placeholder. M11.6 power: 40 h on one AA (Russian goggles not found; PVS-14 class 40 h at 20 C, search extracts; low); 20 s to change the cell (inferred, low); switched on below light 0.5, the night sensor's nightLight, so it is on whenever it helps (review fix 2026-11-16; game value, low). Mass 0.585 kg without the cell (0.6 kg with it, as before).
M11.6: one AA lithium cell for the night-vision goggle (PVS-14 class goggles run on 1x AA; Russian goggles' power not found); charge in Wh (~4 Wh, 15 g). Low, owner to review.

Section radio, typical mass (0.9 kg with its battery). M11.6 power: 8 h on a battery pack (R-187 family rated up to 12 h, search extracts; shorter for combat duty: inferred, low); 10 s to change it (inferred, low). The battery is a separate item now: mass 0.55 kg without it (0.9 kg with it, as before).

M11.6: battery pack of the R-187P1 Azart handheld; charge in Wh. The R-187 family is rated up to 12 h (search extracts, not the P1 specifically); the radio's power.hours is 8 for combat duty with more transmitting (inferred, low). Capacity ~30 Wh and mass 0.35 kg inferred (466 g bare, ~900 g with battery and antenna, cryptomuseum extract): low, owner to review.
The BMP-2's fuel tank (M7): the charge is litres of diesel (0.84 kg per litre). The tank itself is part of the hull (mass 0). Capacity is a game value.
The BMP-2's armour-piercing ready belt: 160 rounds (published total 500 in two belts; the split is commonly quoted, low).
The BMP-2's high-explosive ready belt: 340 rounds (see the AP belt).
250-round belt for the PKT, every fourth round tracer (game value).
Game value: one charge of the vehicle's fire extinguishing system (M7.4b).

One 9M113M missile in its launch container (tube): the launcher holds one, the BMP-2 carries four in all (published: four rounds, reloaded through the gunner's hatch). Container mass (about 10 kg empty) is a game value.

Elastic rubber (Esmarch / Alfa type) tourniquet of the Russian kit (nordsint.org, search extract). UK Defence Intelligence 2023: 'inappropriate use of the crude in-service Russian combat tourniquet' a leading cause of preventable deaths (forcesnews, search extract). Owner: about 1.4x the time and 0.8x the success of the CAT (item factors).
Individual dressing packet IPP-1 (nordsint.org, search extract). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Haemostatic powder ('Gemostop' type) of the Russian kit (nordsint.org, search extract). Owner: about 1.4x the time and 0.8x the success of gauze.
Syringe tube with an opioid (promedol) of the Russian kit (nordsint.org, search extract). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Rescue blanket (rifleman-medic's bag; proposal). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.

Stretcher (носилки санитарные) of the stretcher bearers (санитары-носильщики, research 2026-11-14 studfile.net extract on medical support in battle). Not issued to anyone on the map yet: bearers come from off the map (owner Q-1c). Mass a game value. Not used up.

The rifleman-medic's (strelok-sanitar) bag, empty; contents counted in his load (three rubber tourniquets, six dressings, two haemostatic powders, two pain syringe tubes, a rescue blanket). Proposal: kit not found beyond the individual one (research 2026-11-14).

Red cross armband: marks the wearer as medical personnel (GC I art. 40; Russia uses the red cross emblem). Worn by the BMM ambulance crew (review fix 2026-11-15: medical transport personnel are protected while not fighting). Not issued to the strelok-sanitar, a rifleman with first-aid duties (not exclusively medical personnel).
The BMM's fuel tank (M10.6-data): the charge is litres of diesel (0.84 kg per litre); 290 L as quoted for the BTR-80 (search extracts). The tank is part of the hull (mass 0).
Game value: one charge of the vehicle's fire extinguishing system.

Thermal weapon sight (M9.2): Ratnik lists 1PN140/1PN141 night and thermal sights, and its night-vision parts have very limited distribution (search extracts). Research default, low (owner round M9 screen 3 (a)): one per platoon, with the platoon commander. Mass is a game value. M11.6 power: 5 h (1PN139/1PN140 not found; like AA/CR123 clip-on thermals, 4-6.5 h: inferred, low); 15 s to change the set (inferred, low); always on (it magnifies and sees heat by day too, so it drains by day: review fix 2026-11-16; game value, low). Mass 0.955 kg without the cells (1 kg with them, as before).
M11.6: battery set of the thermal weapon sight (1PN139/1PN140 power not found; assumed 3 AA lithium cells like clip-on thermals, ~12 Wh, 45 g). Low, owner to review.
Thermal (multispectral) camouflage cape (M9.2): a still man under it shows a quarter of his heat to a thermal sight. Game values; not issued to anyone by default.

2B14 Podnos, M8.3a: 82 mm, 42 kg, crew 4, range 80-85 m to 4,270 m, up to 24 rounds a minute (Wikipedia and weaponsystems.net, search extracts; a 2024 MoD-linked report gives 15-22 per minute); man-portable in three loads or carried by a vehicle. Sustained one round every 4 s, set-up 60 s, packing 30 s, crewMin 2, aim error 15 m, dispersion 10 m per km, processing 25 s, flight 8 s + 6 s per km and heard out to 3 km are game values.

2B11 of the 2S12 Sani complex, M8.3a: 120 mm, range 480 m to 7,100 m (OF-843B), 10 rounds a minute normal, 15 maximum, crew 5 (Rostec via Army Recognition; Wikipedia: 4 gunners and a commander), carried on a GAZ-66-based truck (2F510) with the 2L81 wheeled carriage (search extracts). Mass about 210 kg, set-up 120 s, packing 60 s, sustained a round every 6 s, crewMin 2, aim error 15 m, dispersion 8 m per km, processing 30 s, flight 10 s + 6 s per km, heard out to 4 km: game values. The truck is not modelled: the section starts at its position.

One 9M131 missile in its launch tube (published: 13.8 kg in the tube); the split into an 11 kg missile and a 2.8 kg tube is a game value. Counted item (rule 9): the team takes one out of a man's load at each launch.

9P151 launch post of the 9K115-2 Metis-M (M9.3b): 10.2 kg (search extracts; 9.5 kg for the Metis-M1's 9P151M), carried by the team's gunner. The crewServed block: set-up 15 s, packing 8 s, crew 3 (the real crew is two; the third man of the company's team carries rounds: game organisation), the fewest who can still fire 1, sight 1.0 m above the ground (kneeling behind the raised tripod), danger zone 20 m behind, launch heard out to 600 m, traverse +-30 deg before a 3 s re-lay, 2 s to lay on a target: game values (low).

M9.4a (owner M9 round: one quadcopter at the platoon HQ): a commercial Mavic 3T class quadcopter, widely reported in Russian units (search extracts: 920 g, up to 45 min flight, 38 min hover, 21 m/s top speed, 640 x 512 thermal camera). Its operator is an added man in the platoon HQ (low). Control range kept to 3 km in the game (radio link over terrain; jamming M14). Cruise speed, noise and camera values are game values.
M9.4a: the quadcopter's flight battery; charge in Wh (Mavic 3 class: 77 Wh; DE a game value). Three per drone (game value, low).

The Russian serviceman's personal tag (lichny znak, a metal plate with the personal number; Order of the Minister of Defence No. 500 of 5 Nov 2000, search extracts only): one piece, not halved. Mass about 15 g: typical value (low).

One 125 mm 3BM60 round (projectile and charge as one item; M7.6a, game value).
